pages.summary: The class of a value, and whether a value is of a class or a category of classes.
body: `class` gives the name: `'double'`, `'char'`, `'cell'`, `'struct'`, `'int8'`, `'logical'`, `'function_handle'`, a class of your own, .... `isa(x, name)` is true when x is of that class, or of one derived from it, or of a category: `'numeric'` (the number classes), `'float'` (double and single) or `'integer'` (the integer classes).

pages.summary: Tests of a value's class: a number, a floating-point number, an integer class, logical, a character array, a string array.
body: `isinteger` is about the class, not the value: `isinteger(5)` is false, since 5 is a double. Logical values and characters are not numeric.
syntax: double, single or an integer class.

examples.title: The same tests on five values
examples.code:
v = {5, single(5), int8(5), true, 'a'};
cellfun(@isnumeric, v)
cellfun(@isfloat, v)
cellfun(@isinteger, v)
cellfun(@islogical, v)
[ischar('a') ischar("a") isstring("a")]

pages.summary: Values converted to single precision: 32-bit floating point, about 7 significant digits.
body: Half the memory of double and less precise: `eps('single')` is about 1.2e-7. Arithmetic of single with double gives single.

pages.summary: Values converted to integer classes: rounded to the nearest whole number, and held within the class's range.
body: Signed classes (`int8` to `int64`) hold negative numbers, unsigned (`uint8` to `uint64`) do not; the number gives the bits. A value outside the range saturates at its end (`intmin`, `intmax`), NaN becomes 0, and halves round away from zero. Integer arithmetic stays in the class, rounding each result, and integers combine only with doubles and the same class.
syntax: 8-bit unsigned: 0 to 255 (and so on for 16, 32 and 64 bits).

pages.summary: Numbers converted to logical values: nonzero is true.
body: Logical values index arrays by position (`x(logical([1 0 1]))` picks the first and third). NaN cannot be converted.

pages.summary: Values converted to a class by name, numbers' bytes read as another class, and the bytes of each element reversed.
body: `cast(x, classname)` converts as the class's own function does (`'like', p` takes p's class). `typecast` keeps the bytes and reads them as another numeric class: four uint8 values become one uint32, a double becomes eight bytes. `swapbytes` reverses each element's bytes, between big-endian and little-endian.

examples.title: Converted, reinterpreted, and swapped
examples.code:
cast(3.7, 'int16')
cast(5, 'like', single(1))
typecast(uint8([1 0 0 0]), 'uint32')
typecast(single(1), 'uint32')
swapbytes(uint16(1))

pages.summary: Function handles as text and from text, and what a handle holds.
body: `func2str` gives the handle's text (`'sin'`, or `'@(x)x.^2'` for an anonymous function); `str2func` makes a handle from a name or the text of an anonymous function. `functions` gives a struct describing the handle: its function, its type, and for an anonymous function the values it captured.

ans =

ans =

ans =

pages.summary: The variables an expression uses, sorted.
body: The names in a text expression, other than the functions there are and the constants `i`, `j`, `pi`, `Inf`, `NaN` and `eps`; for a symbolic expression, its symbolic variables.

pages.summary: A function called by handle or by name.
body: `feval(f, x1, x2)` is `f(x1, x2)`; the function may be given as text, which is how a function chosen at run time is called. A fit from `fit` is evaluated at x.

examples.title: By name, by handle, and several outputs
examples.code:
feval('max', [3 9 2])
feval(@(x, y) x + y, 2, 3)
[m, i] = feval('max', [3 9 2])
names = {'sin', 'cos'};
cellfun(@(n) feval(n, 0), names)

pages.summary: The members of an enumeration class.
body: A class with an `enumeration` block has a fixed set of members, each an object: `Color.Red`, `Color.Green`. They compare with `==` (and with their names as text), work in `switch` and `ismember`, and give their names with `char` and `string`. A class based on a number class (`classdef Level < uint8`) has members that are those numbers.

pages.summary: A package's functions and classes called by their short names.
body: A package is a folder whose name starts with `+`: `+geo/dist.m` is the function `geo.dist`, `+geo/+util/f.m` is `geo.util.f`. `import geo.*` lets the code that follows call `dist` alone; `import geo.dist` that one name. An import in a function lasts for that call; one in the Command Window until it is restarted. `import` alone lists them.
